title: Grateful Dead Live at Frost Amphitheatre - Stanford University on 1982-10-09
lineage: Cassette Master (Nakamichi DR-1/Dolby B) -> Sound Devices 744T (24bit/88.2k) -> Samplitude Professional v10.1 -> FLAC/24 (1 DVD FLAC)
source: (FOB) Sony ECM-220T -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Fuji Metal Tape/Dolby B)

ai_review.summary: A spectacular audience tape captured with Sony ECM220T mics that showcases a tight 1982 Frost performance, highlighted by an unforgettable Touch of Grey.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised for its crystal‑clear capture despite being an older AUD source—thanks to the legendary Sony ECM‑220T microphones—though some note vocals sit a little high in the mix. Musically the show is described as tight and special, with the band firing on all cylinders and the Touch of Grey standing out as a funky, vocal‑driven highlight. A few reviewers mention a rushed ending and Phil’s bass sounding muted for this era, but overall the performance is celebrated.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviews give 5‑star ratings praising both the music and the surprisingly good AUD recording; only a few lower scores note minor issues, resulting in an overall strong weighted average.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Sony ECM‑220T mics deliver crisp, clear capture for an audience tape; occasional comments about vocals being prominent but no major dropouts or distortion.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Opening shows of the tour at a beautiful venue; tight playing throughout with a strong first set and a slightly rushed ending.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His vocal on Touch of Grey is described as funky and enjoyable; guitar tone not specifically mentioned but overall performance praised.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass tone noted as muffled, flat, and lacking the usual punch of earlier years, which detracts from the mix.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent's Yamaha CP‑70 sounds weak and flat compared to his classic Rhodes, described as a 'toy piano' quality.
